I thought the design was to use 3D luts in master and I wasn't sure of a design that allows both.

Edited: As far as I know 3D LUTs are the more common format. (They're generated from a 2d image that is split.)

There is a workflow that converts .CUBE to pngs.

https://www.redsharknews.com/post-vfx/item/2966-the-beginners-guide-to-luts Mentioned that 2D LUTS do not exist.

LUT already experiment the result well --> https://youtu.be/FacL-08WpP8 

already tried the gimp editor handle colors well import godot texture3D --> https://youtu.be/4lYdYqshSmY

I don't think it's the responsibility of this pr to write this conversion. I imagined that there was a way to convert Texture2D into a Texture3D using default settings of 8 tiles width and 8 tiles height. 

A restart is required to convert a Texture2D to a Texture3D. A Texture2D that is 2D can be converted to a Texture3D of like 64x64x1 which is 1 Tile width and 1 Tile depth compared to a regular Texture3D that is a 2D image converted to 64x64x64 which is 8 tiles width and 8 tiles height by default. Then, bi-linear interpolation from the 3D Material should function. I don't have any examples of a 2D LUT to test.

The current workflow for users is that they can create a LUT using a single gradient texture. While it is clear that a 1D LUT is extremely limiting, its what every Godot game uses and it is very easy for users to get something working. They just add a gradient texture and can have results in seconds. 

Switching to a 3D LUT breaks every game that is using the 1D LUT and it makes adding a LUT considerably more difficult as the LUT needs to be generated outside of the engine. 

While I understand that the 3D LUT is much more powerful and expressive (and we need support for them), there has been no discussion about breaking the previous workflow, in particular, there has been no proposal weighing the pros and cons. 

That being said, adding support for texture2Ds and texture3Ds would be easy and would avoid creating breaking changes, so that is what I prefer. Otherwise, we need to find out from users if they are okay losing the current LUT approach.

The workflow for conversion of a 2D LUT would be to turn a png into a 1 tile width and 1 tile height 3d texture, which is doable.

On a related note, I had a hard time finding anyone providing examples for the 2D LUT workflow in Godot Engine.

Did you mean 2D LUT? A 1D LUT is a line. I think you can interpolate a line into a cube.

Edited:

Will show a example of this.

The current approach in (3.2) accepts a Texture2D which represents a 1D LUT. 

I am not suggesting a conversion tool (although a conversion tool is a viable idea). I am suggested allowing users to use the current workflow and the new 3D texture workflow.

issue_context.title: Vulkan: Adjustments (brightness/contrast/saturation) not reimplemented yet
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** Git https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/aded76cb84fd1081279d2ed11fd73b553c6e6b4e

**OS/device including version:** Fedora 31, GeForce GTX 1080 (NVIDIA 440.100)

**Issue description:**

After enabling adjustments in Environment, tweaking brightness/contrast/saturation does nothing.

**Steps to reproduce:**

Enable Adjustments in Environment and tweak the values.

**Minimal reproduction project:** [test_adjustments.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5075212/test_adjustments.zip)

review_comments: This stuff isn't necessary. Since we just pass the RID to the rendering device, all updates happen automatically.
But gradient changing doesn't work. I guess we can document that you need to restart the editor to modify the gradient..
Closing, please reopen if you have arguments why we need to restart the editor to change colours on the gradient colours list.

Did you test it out? You can update the gradient and everything updates automatically. There is no point in sending the same RID to the server over and over again. 

Take a look at the 3.2 code, it worked the same way.
Yes I did. I can give you a video.
https://imgur.com/a/gsVy0zq Here are the two variations of the changes. One has this code removed.
The only one that works is when I connect the gradient changed signal to changing the adjustments.
